key_insight: Gradient-aware AI agents can autonomously propose, train, and revise turbulence closures by coupling LLM-guided discovery with differentiable CFD.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce manual effort in developing turbulence closures tailored to target flow statistics.
method: Use multi-agent LLMs to search analytical, neural, and hybrid closure forms.
Embed proposals in a GPU-native differentiable CFD solver and validate objectives and gradient paths.
Use simulation results and truncated-horizon gradients to optimize parameters and guide subsequent proposals.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D turbulence and 3D channel-flow LES recovered reference coefficients beyond forward-only evaluation within the same budget and improved agreement with targeted reference statistics.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the demonstrated flows remains unestablished, and truncated-horizon gradients may miss longer-term effects.
paper_title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
